'''Lusia Mamedovna Aloeva''' ({{langx|ka|ლუსია ალოევა}}; {{langx|ru|Люся Мамедовна Алоева}}; {{langx|kmr|Lûsîya Aloyêva}}; 28 October 1928 – 18 February 2011) was a [[Yazidism in Georgia|Georgian-Yezidi]] botanist and biologist. A member of Tbilisi's [[Yezidis|Yezidi]] community, she is considered to have been the first female Yezidi scientist. She taught botany for decades at [[Tbilisi State University]], where she became the first Yezidi student and the first Yezidi woman to defend a doctoral dissertation in 1967. She was awarded Georgia's [[Order of Honor (Georgia)|Order of Honor]] in 2003.

== Early life and education ==
Aloeva was born in Tbilisi on 28 October 1928 to a working-class family,<ref name="auto1">{{cite web |title=ლუსია ალოევა (1928–2011) |url=http://www.nplg.gov.ge/bios/en/00018373/ |website=Biographical Dictionary of Georgia |publisher=National Parliamentary Library of Georgia |language=ka |access-date=6 November 2026}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{cite web |last=Ameyan |first=Ekaterina |title=Знаменитые езидки |url=https://www.ezidipress.com/ru/2014/01/31/знаменитые-езидки/ |website=ÊzîdîPress |language=ru |date=31 January 2014 |access-date=6 November 2026}}</ref> and belonged to the priestly caste of [[Yazidi social organization#Pîr|Pîrs]].<ref name="Rodziewicz2026-1">{{Cite book |last=Rodziewicz |first=Artur |title=The yezidis of the south caucasus: their past and present in georgia |date=2026 |publisher=Brill |isbn=978-90-04-76177-3 |edition=Icm |series=Iran and the caucasus monographs |location=Boston |pages=496}}</ref> In 1937, she was accepted to Tbilisi Russian Secondary School No. 100, and from 1942 she studied at Secondary School No. 25, from which she graduated in 1948. That same year, she entered the Biology Faculty of Tbilisi State University (TSU), becoming the first Yezidi student there.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Официальный сайт Духовного совета езидов в Грузии |url=http://yezidi.ge/home.php?cat=2&sub=4&id=228&mode=blog&lang=ru |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625083621/http://yezidi.ge/home.php?cat=2&sub=4&id=228&mode=blog&lang=ru |archive-date=2024-06-25 |access-date=2026-11-06 |website=yezidi.ge}}</ref>

== Career ==
Aloeva graduated from the Faculty of Biology at Tbilisi State University in 1953 and worked there as a laboratory assistant. From 1954 to 1956 she attended the evening division of the [[Marx–Engels–Lenin Institute|University of Marxism–Leninism]]. In 1959 she entered [[Extramural education|extramural]] postgraduate study, which she completed in 1963. In 1967 she defended a doctoral dissertation for the degree of [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate of Biological Sciences]] and became a doctor of biological sciences, becoming the first Yezidi woman to hold the degree.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="Ameyan2016-1" /> From 1968 to 1983 she lectured at the Pushkin Tbilisi State Pedagogical Institute.<ref name="auto1"/> Over time, she received the title of Professor and worked as an active researcher at the University from 1971 to 2011.<ref name="Rodziewicz2026-1" />

She was the author of 32 scientific works.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="Ameyan2016-1">{{cite web |last=Ameyan |first=Ekaterina |title=Эволюция прав женщин в езидском обществе |url=https://www.ezidipress.com/ru/2016/01/06/эволюция-прав-женщин-в-езидском-обществе/ |website=ÊzîdîPress |language=ru |date=6 January 2016 |access-date=6 November 2026}}</ref> In 2003 she compiled a nine-page teaching text on the phylogeny of flowering plants for botany students, published by Tbilisi State University Press and edited by Revaz Gagnidze.<ref>{{cite book |author=Aloeva, Lusia (comp.) |editor-last=Gagnidze |editor-first=Revaz |title=ყვავილოვანი მცენარეების ფილოგენია: ბოტანიკის სპეც. სტუდ. |trans-title=Phylogeny of Flowering Plants: for Botany Specialisation Students |location=Tbilisi |publisher=Tbilisi State University Press |year=2003 |page=9 |language=ka}}</ref>  In 2006, she was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in biological sciences. She was the first Yezidi woman to attend university and the first to earn a [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree.<ref name="auto"/> 

== Recognition ==
In 2003 Aloeva received the [[Order of Honor (Georgia)|Order of Honor]] and the [[Ivane Javakhishvili medal]], and she held the title of [[Medal "Veteran of Labour"|Veteran of Labour]].<ref name="auto1"/>
